Big Sys read the card, the code and the tracker first. Her hand-off: Card UHTI: crash in 2H, 5+ Ton rampage, 8,400 log errors. Two leads from reading the code (not yet verified at runtime):

1. IndexOutOfRange + render-property-block exception (spammed together ~6,600x): Assets/Scripts/Rendering/RendererPropertyBlock.cs — StartLerpMaterialSequence(int materialIndex, Material, List<int>, List<int>, float) at line 1155-1162, and LerpMaterial(int materialIndex, ...) at line 1175, both index _materialPropertyCaches[materialIndex] with NO bounds check. The sibling overload at line 1164-1173 DOES check (`if (_materialPropertyCaches.Count <= materialIndex) return;`). Under a heavy rampage (many entities/materials churning), a stale or out-of-range materialIndex reaching either unchecked call site throws IndexOutOfRangeException. Trace callers of these two specific overloads to find where materialIndex can exceed the cache's current count (likely a paint/damage/debris system driving a stored index against a renderer whose material count changed).

2. SpawnHandle leak ("Getting an update for a SpawnHandle but still no bot!", ~800x): Assets/Scripts/Combat/Arena/BotGateBase.cs — AddOrUpdateSpawn (line 182-197). When spawnHandle.haveBot is false, line 193 just logs an error and still overwrites spawnList[existingIdx] = spawnHandle (line 196); the handle is never removed from spawnList or released when a bot fails to spawn. Find where SpawnHandles are allocated/requested for bots about to spawn, and add release/removal for handles whose bot never arrives (timeout or explicit spawn-failure path) — this is the suspected leak under 2H/5+Ton (many simultaneous bot spawns, higher chance some fail).

Attached UHTI log and TheTripleL123's 'minor' commit are on the card for context. Done = both root causes identified/fixed (or ruled out with evidence), and the SpawnHandle leak no longer accumulates on a failed spawn. Verify against a reproduction of the 2H, 5+Ton rampage scenario if possible.
